claim: The Cancer Dependency Map (DepMap) is an ongoing project to uncover gene dependencies in hundreds of cancer cell lines.
source: The Cancer Dependency Map (DepMap) is an ongoing project to uncover these gene dependencies in hundreds of cancer cell lines.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is a description of the DepMap project.

claim: shinyDepMap combines CRISPR and shRNA data to determine gene knockout/knockdown effects on growth and selectivity across cell lines.
source: shinyDepMap combines CRISPR and shRNA data to determine, for each gene, the growth reduction caused by knockout/knockdown and the selectivity of this effect across cell lines.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract as a description of the tool's functionality.

claim: shinyDepMap clusters genes with similar dependencies, revealing functional relationships.
source: The tool also clusters genes with similar dependencies, revealing functional relationships.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a feature of the tool.

claim: Hundreds, if not thousands, of driver mutations cause cancer in different patients.
source: Hundreds, if not thousands, of driver mutations cause cancer in different patients (MC3 Working Group et al., 2018), and extensive collaborative efforts such as the Cancer Genome Atlas Program (TCGA) have helped discover them (The Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Targeted therapies aim to treat cancer by selectively killing cancer cells with a specific genotype and spectrum of driver mutations.
source: Targeted therapies, a type of precision medicine, aim to treat cancer by selectively killing cancer cells with a specific genotype and spectrum of driver mutations (Friedman et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The epidermal growth factor receptor is strongly required in certain cancer cells but not in normal bone marrow stem cells.
source: For example, the epidermal growth factor receptor is strongly required in certain cancer cells, but not in normal bone marrow stem cells, making it a potentially good target (Wang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The DepMap project identifies essential genes across hundreds of cancer cell lines using genome-wide CRISPR and shRNA screens.
source: The Cancer Dependency Map (DepMap) is an ongoing project to identify essential genes across hundreds of cancer cell lines using genome-wide CRISPR and shRNA screens (Tsherniak et al., 2017; Behan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: DepMap data has been used successfully to discover cancer cells' genetic vulnerabilities.
source: It has already been used successfully to discover cancer cells' genetic vulnerabilities (Sandoval et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2019b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: The DepMap portal website has no native tools to integrate CRISPR and shRNA or to examine functional relationships among essential genes beyond pairwise comparisons.
source: However, the DepMap portal has no native tools to integrate CRISPR and shRNA or to examine functional relationships among essential genes beyond pairwise comparisons.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the limitations of the existing DepMap portal.

claim: 15,847 genes were tested in 423 cell lines with both CRISPR and shRNA methods.
source: To assess the consistency between CRISPR and shRNA dependency scores, we first compared the gene/cell line combinations tested with both methods (15,847 genes in 423 cell lines, Figure 1—source data 1) and computed essentiality thresholds for each distribution such that a dependency score more negative than the threshold is considered essential (Figure 1A; 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section and refers to data analysis.

claim: CRISPR and shRNA methods showed a Pearson correlation of 0.456 and Spearman correlation of 0.201 in dependency scores.
source: The two methods were somewhat consistent on average, with both methods yielding approximately normal dependency score distributions with mean zero and a left-skewing tail corresponding to the subset of essential genes (Pearson correlation 0.456, Spearman correlation 0.201).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: CRISPR tends to detect weak to moderate gene deletion effects more sensitively than shRNA.
source: First, CRISPR tends to detect weak to moderate gene deletion effects more sensitively, as evidenced by the greater density of CRISPR-essential genes above the diagonal in the joint distribution plot (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to Figure 1A.

claim: 958 genes were claimed commonly essential only by CRISPR but not by shRNA.
source: We found that 958 and 20 genes were claimed commonly essential only by CRISPR or shRNA, respectively (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 1C.

claim: 20 genes were claimed commonly essential only by shRNA but not by CRISPR.
source: We found that 958 and 20 genes were claimed commonly essential only by CRISPR or shRNA, respectively (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 1C.

claim: tRNA metabolic process and mitochondrial translation are overrepresented in the CRISPR-only essential gene set.
source: Notably, these two sets of inconsistently essential genes are enriched for involvement in distinct pathways: for example, tRNA metabolic process and mitochondrial translation are overrepresented in the CRISPR-only set, whereas cytosolic translation initiation is overrepresented in the shRNA-only set (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and refers to Figure 1D showing pathway enrichment analysis.

claim: Cytosolic translation initiation is overrepresented in the shRNA-only essential gene set.
source: Notably, these two sets of inconsistently essential genes are enriched for involvement in distinct pathways: for example, tRNA metabolic process and mitochondrial translation are overrepresented in the CRISPR-only set, whereas cytosolic translation initiation is overrepresented in the shRNA-only set (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and refers to Figure 1D showing pathway enrichment analysis.

claim: CRISPR and shRNA have distinct biases in assessing some genes' essentiality, affecting different classes of genes.
source: This suggests that CRISPR and shRNA have distinct biases in assessing some genes' essentiality, affecting different classes of genes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the pathway enrichment analysis results.

claim: CRISPR is considered to be less susceptible to off-target effects than shRNA.
source: While CRISPR is considered to be less susceptible to off-target effects (Smith et al., 2017) and thus now generally preferred over shRNA, the results and their therapeutic relevance may also depend on the genes of interest.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: EIF5B is highly conserved throughout Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya, suggesting it may be essential for most human cells.
source: For example, EIF5B, a gene involved in translation initiation, is highly conserved throughout Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya, suggesting that it may be essential for most human cells (Sørensen et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Only shRNA, but not CRISPR, highlighted EIF5B as an essential gene.
source: However, only shRNA, but not CRISPR, highlighted it as an essential gene.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as an observation from the data.

claim: X=1 was selected for most of the analysis, equivalent to claiming a gene essential when roughly 5 out of 423 cell lines show dependence on the gene.
source: We selected X=1 for most of our analysis. This is equivalent to claiming a gene essential when roughly 5 out of 423 cell lines show dependence on the gene (p=7.8e-5, binomial test).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the parameter choice and its statistical interpretation.

claim: Only 56% (2037 genes) of the essential genes overlapped between CRISPR (SC) and shRNA (SR) methods.
source: Reflecting the inconsistencies between CRISPR and shRNA, only 56% (2037 genes) of the essential genes overlapped between SC and SR (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 2D.

claim: Genes with strongly negative efficacy tend to be less selective.
source: By comparing the efficacy and selectivity, we found that genes with strongly negative efficacy tend to be less selective, whereas selectively essential genes tend to have only moderate efficacy (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 3C.

claim: Selectively essential genes tend to have only moderate efficacy.
source: By comparing the efficacy and selectivity, we found that genes with strongly negative efficacy tend to be less selective, whereas selectively essential genes tend to have only moderate efficacy (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 3C.

claim: Chromatin regulation is overrepresented among genes that are both selective and essential.
source: For example, chromatin regulation is overrepresented among genes that are both selective and essential; nuclear metabolism and translation are overrepresented among essential (but not selective) genes; and regulation of kinase activity and tissue development are overrepresented among selective (but not essential) genes (Figure 3D, Figure 3D—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 3D.

claim: Nuclear metabolism and translation are overrepresented among essential (but not selective) genes.
source: For example, chromatin regulation is overrepresented among genes that are both selective and essential; nuclear metabolism and translation are overrepresented among essential (but not selective) genes; and regulation of kinase activity and tissue development are overrepresented among selective (but not essential) genes (Figure 3D, Figure 3D—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 3D.

claim: Regulation of kinase activity and tissue development are overrepresented among selective (but not essential) genes.
source: For example, chromatin regulation is overrepresented among genes that are both selective and essential; nuclear metabolism and translation are overrepresented among essential (but not selective) genes; and regulation of kinase activity and tissue development are overrepresented among selective (but not essential) genes (Figure 3D, Figure 3D—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 3D.

claim: Lower selectivity and more negative efficacy are associated with a greater number of dependent cell lines.
source: For each gene, we assessed the relationship between the number of cell lines dependent on the gene and the gene's efficacy and selectivity, and confirmed that lower selectivity and more negative efficacy and are associated with a greater number of dependent cell lines (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 4A.

claim: A greater number of dependent lineages was associated with more negative efficacy and lower selectivity.
source: As with dependent cell lines, a greater number of dependent lineages was associated with more negative efficacy and lower selectivity (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 4B.

claim: 1050 genes are commonly essential across all the lineages.
source: Overall, we found that 1050 genes are commonly essential across all the lineages, 670 genes are essential in at least one lineage, and 2581 essential genes were not lineage-dependent (Figure 4B, C, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 4B, C.

claim: 670 genes are essential in at least one lineage.
source: Overall, we found that 1050 genes are commonly essential across all the lineages, 670 genes are essential in at least one lineage, and 2581 essential genes were not lineage-dependent (Figure 4B, C, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 4B, C.

claim: 2581 essential genes were not lineage-dependent.
source: Overall, we found that 1050 genes are commonly essential across all the lineages, 670 genes are essential in at least one lineage, and 2581 essential genes were not lineage-dependent (Figure 4B, C, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 4B, C.

claim: The number of dependent cell lines is strongly associated with the number of dependent lineages.
source: Unsurprisingly, the number of dependent cell lines is strongly associated with the number of dependent lineages (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 4C.

claim: Most genes with high selectivity scores were also identified as targets for one or more lineages in Behan et al.'s analysis.
source: We found that most genes with high selectivity scores were also identified as targets for one or more lineages in their analysis (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 4D, comparing results with published work.

claim: Lineage specificity is not the only cause of high selectivity.
source: Though we saw a strong relationship between lower selectivity and a greater number of dependent cell lines and lineages (Figure 4A, B), we note that lineage specificity is not the only cause of high selectivity.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as an interpretation of the results.

claim: CTNNB1 shows broad dependence in colorectal cancer.
source: Some genes do manifest this type of selectivity (e.g., broad dependence on CTNNB1 in colorectal cancer, MYB in leukemia, IRF4 in multiple myeloma, KRAS in pancreatic cancer, and SOX10 in skin cancer, Figure 4E)
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 4E.

claim: MYB shows broad dependence in leukemia.
source: Some genes do manifest this type of selectivity (e.g., broad dependence on CTNNB1 in colorectal cancer, MYB in leukemia, IRF4 in multiple myeloma, KRAS in pancreatic cancer, and SOX10 in skin cancer, Figure 4E)
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 4E.

claim: IRF4 shows broad dependence in multiple myeloma.
source: Some genes do manifest this type of selectivity (e.g., broad dependence on CTNNB1 in colorectal cancer, MYB in leukemia, IRF4 in multiple myeloma, KRAS in pancreatic cancer, and SOX10 in skin cancer, Figure 4E)
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 4E.

claim: KRAS shows broad dependence in pancreatic cancer.
source: Some genes do manifest this type of selectivity (e.g., broad dependence on CTNNB1 in colorectal cancer, MYB in leukemia, IRF4 in multiple myeloma, KRAS in pancreatic cancer, and SOX10 in skin cancer, Figure 4E)
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 4E.

claim: SOX10 shows broad dependence in skin cancer.
source: Some genes do manifest this type of selectivity (e.g., broad dependence on CTNNB1 in colorectal cancer, MYB in leukemia, IRF4 in multiple myeloma, KRAS in pancreatic cancer, and SOX10 in skin cancer, Figure 4E)
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 4E.

claim: CDK4 is not commonly essential in any lineages but is selectively essential in many.
source: CDK4 is a particularly strong example of this pattern as it is not commonly essential in any lineages, but is selectively essential in many.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as an observation from the data.

claim: When a set of genes comprise a functional unit that regulates cell viability, these genes would be expected to have similar dependency profiles.
source: When a set of genes comprise a functional unit (e.g., a pathway or a complex) that regulates cell viability, these genes would be expected to have similar dependency profiles.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the expected behavior of functionally related genes.

claim: The clustering approach is based on t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) and density-based spatial clustering and noise (DBSCAN).
source: Our approach is based on a related pair of popular algorithms, t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE), and density-based spatial clustering and noise (DBSCAN) (van der Maaten and Hinton, 2008; van der Maaten, 2014; Ester et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to the original algorithms.

claim: t-SNE has been widely used for visualizing high-dimensional data, such as single-cell RNA-seq data.
source: It has been widely used for visualizing high-dimensional data, such as single-cell RNA-seq data (Mass et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The combination of t-SNE and DBSCAN is a powerful clustering algorithm for high-dimensional data, such as single-cell transcriptomes.
source: The combination of t-SNE and DBSCAN (expressed as 't-SNE + DBSCAN' hereafter) is a powerful clustering algorithm for high-dimensional data, such as single-cell transcriptomes (Haber et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The t-SNE algorithm is stochastic, producing different results and clusters with different initial seeds.
source: One limitation of this approach is that the t-SNE algorithm is stochastic, producing different results and clusters with different initial seeds.
evidence: This is a statement about a known property of the t-SNE algorithm.

claim: Strongly positively correlated points are always clustered together while weakly positively correlated points are less consistently so when comparing clusters from multiple t-SNE + DBSCAN runs.
source: However, when we compared clusters yielded by t-SNE + DBSCAN from multiple runs, we found that strongly positively correlated points are always clustered together while weakly positively correlated points are less consistently so.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the analysis.

claim: ECHODOTS runs t-SNE with different initial seeds 200 times.
source: Briefly, ECHODOTS consists of four steps (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1): it (1) computes the pairwise Spearman distance matrix among essential genes, (2) feeds the distance matrix as input to run t-SNE with different initial seeds 200 times, (3) clusters data points based on their coordinates in the t-SNE plot with DBSCAN, and (4) identifies the sets of genes assigned to the same cluster consistently across the 200 sets of clusters using a technique called ensemble clustering (Hornik, 2005).
evidence: This is a direct description of the ECHODOTS algorithm.

claim: ECHODOTS produces more reliable clusters than a single run of t-SNE + DBSCAN by seeking data points that are consistently clustered together.
source: ECHODOTS produces more reliable clusters than a single run of t-SNE + DBSCAN by seeking data points that are consistently clustered together.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion about the method's performance.

claim: Genes in the same cluster tended to be close to each other on t-SNE maps from individual runs.
source: Genes in the same cluster tended to be close to each other on t-SNE maps from individual runs, and some clusters were enriched for genes known to be members of specific biological pathways or complexes (Figure 5B, Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 5B.

claim: Some clusters were enriched for genes known to be members of specific biological pathways or complexes.
source: Genes in the same cluster tended to be close to each other on t-SNE maps from individual runs, and some clusters were enriched for genes known to be members of specific biological pathways or complexes (Figure 5B, Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 5B.

claim: KEAP1 and KCTD10 are both strongly correlated with the E3 ubiquitin ligase CUL3 but have no correlation with each other.
source: In this cluster, KEAP1 and KCTD10 are both strongly correlated with the E3 ubiquitin ligase CUL3 (with correlations of 0.387 and 0.29, respectively), but have no correlation with each other (correlation −0.002).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with specific correlation values.

claim: KEAP1 and KCTD10 interact with CUL3 in a mutually exclusive manner, both serving as adaptor proteins binding the same site on CUL3 but the resulting complexes degrade distinct target proteins.
source: This is likely due to the fact that KEAP1 and KCTD10 interact with CUL3 in a mutually exclusive manner: both serve as adaptor proteins binding the same site on CUL3 but the resulting complexes degrade distinct target proteins (NFE2L2 and RHOB, respectively) (Cullinan et al., 2004; Kovačević et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Cluster L119 comprises three small clusters, with S369 and S745 containing core MAP kinase (MAPK) pathway proteins and S641 consisting of CTNNB1 and TCF7L2.
source: One is cluster L119 (Figure 5F), which comprises three small clusters. Clusters S369 and S745 contain the core MAP kinase (MAPK) pathway proteins, including KRAS, RAF1, BRAF, and MAPK1, while cluster S641 consists of CTNNB1 (β-catenin) and TCF7L2, which form a bipartite transcription factor complex that is a key effector of the Wnt signaling pathway (Jin and Liu, 2008).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 5F.

claim: CTNNB1 and TCF7L2 form a bipartite transcription factor complex that is a key effector of the Wnt signaling pathway.
source: Clusters S369 and S745 contain the core MAP kinase (MAPK) pathway proteins, including KRAS, RAF1, BRAF, and MAPK1, while cluster S641 consists of CTNNB1 (β-catenin) and TCF7L2, which form a bipartite transcription factor complex that is a key effector of the Wnt signaling pathway (Jin and Liu, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The clustering suggests that MAPK and Wnt signaling are functionally related in dependent cancer cell lines.
source: These small clusters are within the same large cluster, suggesting that MAPK and Wnt signaling are functionally related in dependent cancer cell lines (Jeong et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference from the clustering results, supported by a citation.

claim: SHOC2 was positively correlated to KRAS, RAF1, BRAF, and MAPK1.
source: Cluster L119 also contains SHOC2, which was positively correlated to KRAS, RAF1, BRAF, and MAPK1.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as an observation from the data.

claim: Multiple KRAS-mutant cancers were recently shown to be vulnerable to the loss of SHOC2 in the context of MEK inhibition.
source: Multiple KRAS-mutant cancers were recently shown to be vulnerable to the loss of SHOC2 in the context of MEK inhibition, confirming the link between SHOC2 and MAP kinase pathway-driven cancers (Sulahian et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Cluster S154 contains the selenoprotein GPX4 and genes involved in selenoprotein synthesis (SEPHS2, SEPSECS, PSTK, EFFSEC).
source: Cluster S154 contains the selenoprotein GPX4. GPX4 encodes glutathione peroxidase 4, an antioxidant enzyme, that reduces cytotoxic lipid peroxides and protects cells from a non-apoptotic cell death, called ferroptosis. Intriguingly, we found that the other genes in cluster S154 were involved in selenoprotein synthesis (SEPHS2, SEPSECS, PSTK, EFFSEC) (Squires and Berry, 2008)
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with a citation.

claim: GPX4 encodes glutathione peroxidase 4, an antioxidant enzyme that reduces cytotoxic lipid peroxides and protects cells from ferroptosis.
source: GPX4 encodes glutathione peroxidase 4, an antioxidant enzyme, that reduces cytotoxic lipid peroxides and protects cells from a non-apoptotic cell death, called ferroptosis.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge.

claim: The primary role of selenoprotein synthesis genes in dependent cell lines is to synthesize GPX4.
source: Intriguingly, we found that the other genes in cluster S154 were involved in selenoprotein synthesis (SEPHS2, SEPSECS, PSTK, EFFSEC) (Squires and Berry, 2008), suggesting that the primary role of these genes in dependent cell lines is to synthesize GPX4.
evidence: This is an inference from the clustering results and known gene functions.

claim: Cluster L91 represents a gene set related to the sensitivity to ferroptosis.
source: Overall, L91 seems to represent a gene set related to the sensitivity to ferroptosis (Abdalkader et al., 2018; Ingold et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference from the clustering results, supported by citations.

claim: The number of dependent cell lines and the number of dependent lineages per gene increased with larger θ.
source: Consistently, the number of dependent cell lines and the number of dependent lineages per gene increased with larger θ (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B–F).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 5—figure supplement 2B–F.

claim: Larger θ gave more genes with high selectivity.
source: For selectivity, larger θ gave more genes with high selectivity (Figure 5—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 5—figure supplement 2G.

claim: No pathways were associated with selective or both selective and essential genes when θ < 0.5.
source: However, no pathways were associated with selective or both selective and essential genes when θ < 0.5, suggesting that a high selectivity was given to genes more randomly (Figure 5—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 5—figure supplement 2H.

claim: θ = 0.6 was a reasonable choice because the combined dependency score is more informative with more weight on CRISPR than shRNA while having some contribution from shRNA is more beneficial than CRISPR alone.
source: Through the comparison, we concluded that our initial choice of θ = 0.6 was a reasonable one since the combined dependency score is more informative with more weight on CRISPR than shRNA (θ > 0.5, Figure 5—figure supplement 3) while having some contribution from shRNA is more beneficial than CRISPR alone (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the comparative analysis.

claim: shinyDepMap is written in R using the shiny package for building interactive visualization tools.
source: shinyDepMap is written in R (Chang et al., 2019) using the shiny package for building interactive visualization tools.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the implementation of the tool.

claim: shinyDepMap consists of two apps: 'Gene essentiality' and 'Gene cluster'.
source: It consists of two apps: 'Gene essentiality' and 'Gene cluster'.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the structure of the tool.

claim: shinyDepMap can be used via the website https://labsyspharm.shinyapps.io/depmap, by downloading code from GitHub, or by running a Docker container.
source: shinyDepMap can be used in three ways: (1) via the website https://labsyspharm.shinyapps.io/depmap, (2) by downloading the code and preprocessed data from the GitHub repository (Shimada, 2021) and running it on a local computer, and (3) running the app from a Docker container using the image at https://hub.docker.com/r/labsyspharm/shinydepmap.
evidence: This is a direct statement about how to access the tool.

claim: The DepMap data characterizes the genetic requirements for cells grown in culture, which differs from the in vivo tumor environment in critical ways.
source: The DepMap data characterizes the genetic requirements for cells grown in culture, which differs from the in vivo tumor environment in critical ways: the presence of nutrient-rich media, a two-dimensional rather than a three-dimensional substrate, and the lack of a functional immune system or physiological microenvironment.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the DepMap dataset.

claim: The effects of genetic perturbations (knockdown and knockout) do not necessarily correspond to those of chemical inhibition.
source: In addition, the effects of genetic perturbations (knockdown and knockout) do not necessarily correspond to those of chemical inhibition, a discrepancy that makes target identification from datasets like the DepMap less straightforward (Weiss et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation, supported by a citation.

claim: The DepMap includes only cultured cancer lines and no wild-type cell lines or tissues.
source: Finally, because the DepMap includes only cultured cancer lines and no wild-type cell lines or tissues, a highly selective gene in our analysis is not guaranteed to be less toxic to normal tissues when inhibited.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the DepMap dataset.

claim: A highly selective gene in the DepMap analysis is not guaranteed to be less toxic to normal tissues when inhibited.
source: Finally, because the DepMap includes only cultured cancer lines and no wild-type cell lines or tissues, a highly selective gene in our analysis is not guaranteed to be less toxic to normal tissues when inhibited.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation and inference from the dataset composition.

claim: The CRISPR and shRNA efficacy data provided by the DepMap project were normalized with CERES and DEMETER2 algorithms by the Broad Institute, respectively.
source: The CRISPR and shRNA efficacy data provided by the DepMap project were normalized with CERES and DEMETER2 algorithms by the Broad Institute, respectively.

claim: 1,345,642 conditions (20%) were tested using CRISPR but not shRNA.
source: In total, 1,345,642 conditions (20%) were tested using CRISPR, but not shRNA.

claim: 19,001 conditions (0.28%) were tested using shRNA but not CRISPR.
source: Also, 19,001 (0.28%) were tested using shRNA, but not CRISPR.

claim: 4457 conditions (0.066%) were not tested by either CRISPR or shRNA.
source: In total, 4457 (0.066%) conditions were not tested by either CRISPR or shRNA, which were left as missing.

source: In these cases, the missing values were imputed from the other data using local polynomial regression (loess) function in R.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: ECHODOTS performs a soft clustering that can assign each gene to more than one cluster.
source: On the other hand, ECHODOTS performs a soft clustering that can assign each gene to more than one cluster.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section as a property of the algorithm.

claim: ECHODOTS conducts the 'majority vote' among 200 runs of the clustering and computes the probability of a point being assigned to each cluster.
source: It conducts the 'majority vote' among 200 runs of the clustering and computes the probability of a point being assigned to each cluster, which provides us with the strength of evidence for the cluster assignment of each gene.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section as a description of the algorithm.

evidence: This is stated directly in the text and refers to Figure 1B.

source: S572 contains another selenoprotein TXNRD1 and its substrate, TXNDC17 (Espinosa and Arnér, 2019), both of which are also strongly correlated with four selenoprotein synthesis genes.
